alphabet-armenien.title: The Armenian alphabet: 36 letters created in 405 by Mesrop Mashtots #Armenia
alphabet-armenien.description:
Created in 405 by Saint Mesrop Mashtots, the Armenian alphabet gave the language its written form and shaped more than sixteen centuries of literary and calligraphic tradition.

Full article: https://armenianews.org/culture/alphabet-armenien/?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=video

ani.title: Ani, the “City of 1,001 Churches”, ancient Armenian capital #Armenia
ani.description:
Capital of the Bagratids from the 10th century, Ani was a great medieval metropolis and the cradle of an innovative architectural school. Its archaeological site has been on the UNESCO World Heritage List since 2016.

aram-khatchatourian.title: Aram Khachaturian, from the Sabre Dance to Spartacus #Armenia
aram-khatchatourian.description:
Born in Tiflis in 1903, Aram Khachaturian created Armenia's first symphony, first concerto and first ballet, building a bridge between Eastern folklore and the symphonic tradition.

Full article: https://armenianews.org/culture/aram-khatchatourian/?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=video

bataille-de-sardarapat.title: Sardarapat, May 1918: the battle that made the First Republic possible #Armenia
bataille-de-sardarapat.description:
Fought from May 21 to 29, 1918, near Yerevan, the Battle of Sardarapat halted the Ottoman invasion and enabled the declaration of the First Republic of Armenia.

Full article: https://armenianews.org/culture/bataille-de-sardarapat/?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=video

charles-aznavour.title: Charles Aznavour, from Paris to National Hero of Armenia #Armenia
charles-aznavour.description:
Son of an Armenian genocide survivor, Charles Aznavour wrote or co-wrote more than a thousand songs, then served Armenia as an ambassador and was named its National Hero.

duduk.title: The duduk, the apricot-wood oboe that made Khachaturian cry #Armenia
duduk.description:
Carved from apricot wood, the duduk is an Armenian double-reed oboe mentioned as early as the 5th century AD. In 2005 UNESCO proclaimed it and its music a Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity.

epopee-de-david-de-sassoun.title: David of Sassoun, the Armenian epic passed down by word of mouth #Armenia
epopee-de-david-de-sassoun.description:
Passed down orally for more than a thousand years, the epic of David of Sassoun tells of four generations of heroes. Since 2012 it has been on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

Full article: https://armenianews.org/culture/epopee-de-david-de-sassoun/?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=video

khatchkar.title: The khachkar, the Armenian cross-stone carved as a tree of life #Armenia
khatchkar.description:
A stele carved with a cross shaped as a tree of life, the khachkar is a hallmark of Armenian art, inscribed by UNESCO in 2010. An estimated 40,000 survive in the Republic of Armenia.

Full article: https://armenianews.org/culture/khatchkar/?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=video

kochari.title: Kochari: the Armenian circle dance practiced for over a thousand years #Armenia
kochari.description:
Born in the Armenian highlands, kochari is a collective circle dance in which dancers imitate the leaping of goats. Armenian kochari has been on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list since 2017.

Full article: https://armenianews.org/culture/kochari/?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=video

komitas.title: Komitas, the priest who collected more than 3,000 Armenian melodies #Armenia
komitas.description:
Priest, composer and ethnomusicologist, Komitas (1869-1935) collected more than three thousand Armenian folk melodies before being broken by the Armenian Genocide.

Full article: https://armenianews.org/culture/komitas/?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=video

lavash.title: Lavash, the Armenian bread that bakes in 15 to 40 seconds #Armenia
lavash.description:
A traditional flatbread baked in a tonir, lavash embodies the history, conviviality and age-old rituals of the Armenian people. It has been inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list since 2014.

matenadaran-et-les-manuscrits-enlumines.title: Yerevan's Matenadaran, guardian of over 17,000 manuscripts #Armenia
matenadaran-et-les-manuscrits-enlumines.description:
On the heights of Yerevan, the Matenadaran holds over 17,000 manuscripts and some 300,000 archival documents. It has been on UNESCO's Memory of the World Register since 1997.

monastere-de-tatev.title: Tatev, the monastery perched above the Vorotan Gorge #Armenia
monastere-de-tatev.description:
In Syunik, southeastern Armenia, Tatev became the seat of the bishopric in the 9th century and, in the 14th, home to a university: one of the most renowned centers of learning in the Armenian world.

sayat-nova-et-la-tradition-des-ashoughs.title: Sayat-Nova, the “King of Songs” of the Armenian troubadours #Armenia
sayat-nova-et-la-tradition-des-ashoughs.description:
Born in Tiflis in 1712, Armenian poet and minstrel Sayat-Nova became royal musician at the Georgian court of Heraclius II. He remains the most dazzling figure in the tradition of the ashughs.

serguei-paradjanov.title: Sergei Parajanov, the filmmaker who never stopped creating #Armenia
serguei-paradjanov.description:
Born in Tbilisi in 1924 into an Armenian family, Sergei Parajanov made Shadows of Forgotten Ancestors and The Color of Pomegranates, and kept creating even in a Soviet prison camp.

tigrane-le-grand-et-l-empire-armenien.title: Tigranes the Great and Armenia “from sea to sea” #Armenia
tigrane-le-grand-et-l-empire-armenien.description:
King from 95 to 55 BC, Tigranes the Great brought Armenia to its zenith: an empire from the Caspian Sea to the Mediterranean, a Greek-inspired capital at Tigranakert, and a peace negotiated with Rome.

temple-paien-de-garni.title: The only Greco-Roman temple still standing in the former USSR 🏛️ #Armenia
temple-paien-de-garni.description:
Garni Temple, built around AD 76–77 by King Tiridates I, toppled by the 1679 earthquake, then rebuilt stone by stone between 1969 and 1975.
